newsitem.title: CHINA: China vows to ensure HK prosperity, stability.
newsitem.headline: China vows to ensure HK prosperity, stability.

text.p: Beijing on Tuesday marked its first day of rule over Hong Kong in 156 years with a pledge to ensure the prosperity of the freewheeling former British colony, promising a better tomorrow for China.

The solemn handover ceremonies in Hong Kong and all-night celebrations in Beijing marked the sweeping away of a century of humiliation for China, the People's Daily, mouthpiece of the Communist Party said in an editorial that coincided with the party's 76th birthday.
"The return of Hong Kong is the first step in implementing the 'one country, two systems' policy," the official Xinhua news agency quoted the newspaper as saying.
"Even more important is to ensure the long-term prosperity and stability of Hong Kong," People's Daily said.

Beijing has promised to allow Hong Kong to keep its capitalist lifestyle for 50 years after China resumed sovereignty under the "one country, two systems" formula devised by the late leader Deng Xiaoping.
The newspaper paid tribute to Deng, who died last February, aged 92. "We deeply miss our beloved Comrade Deng Xiaoping."

Hong Kong's confidence in China's pledge was dented in June, 1989 when Chinese soldiers backed by tanks crushed student-led demonstrations for democracy centred in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, killing hundreds.
Hong Kong democrats and international human rights groups have voiced concerns about Hong Kong's future under communist rule, fearing for human rights and civil liberties.
The People's Daily was confident. "The world will see -- China's tomorrow will be better," it said.
"The Chinese nation will stride ahead with pride into the new century toward the magnificent goal of modernisation," the newspaper said.

"The reunification of China and the revitalisation of the Chinese nation will become a glorious fact in the future," it said, referring to Beijing's next goals -- the return of Macau in 1999 and China's dream of of reunification with Taiwan.
China has been trying to woo rival Taiwan to reunify under the "one country, two systems" formula.

But the Nationalists who fled to Taiwan after losing the Chinese civil war to the Communists in 1949 have rejected Beijing's overtures, insisting that reunification come after China embraces democracy and a free market economy.

The People's Daily sang the praises of the Communist Party for cementing Hong Kong's handover and lauded Deng's daring reforms that transformed a stagnant Stalinist backwater into a fledgling economic powerhouse.
"Without the leadership of the Communist Party of China, the motherland cannot become stronger by the day," it said.
"Without reform and opening up and without the efforts of new China's third generation of leaders... it would have been impossible for Hong Kong to return," the newspaper said.
However, it stressed the significance of the recovery of Hong Kong in wiping out national humiliation at the hands of imperialist foreign powers.
"The Chinese nation has wiped out more than 100 years of humiliation. The time has come to feel proud and elated," the newspaper said of the handover.
"The long-awaited dream of the Chinese nation and the long-cherished wish of generations for Hong Kong's return has been fulfilled."
